# EC48C — Exact encoder-quotient criterion for seedless BRC ROC faces

**Status:** AUTHOR-SIDE MATHEMATICAL DERIVATION + EXACT FINITE-ALPHABET COMPUTER-ASSISTED CERTIFICATE. Not native Result, independent Driver review, Working Truth, Foundation or X6 dynamical theorem.

## Source, observer and target
Let H,Y be finite nonempty sets, with strictly positive p(h,y),q(h,y), independently normalized to 1. BRC here is a finite positive-rational or positive-real weighted source carrier preserving branch labels (h,y), without signed phase cancellation. A seedless K-memory experiment uses an encoder pi(m|h), and then a decoder u(m,y) in [0,1]. Put w(h,y)=sum_m pi(m|h)u(m,y), alpha=sum_(h,y) p(h,y)w(h,y), beta=sum_(h,y) q(h,y)w(h,y). Its region is S_K, while full history yields the zonotope Z=sum_(h,y)[0,(p(h,y),q(h,y))]. The four declared coordinates are (1-alpha,beta,2,2), with depths fixed.

At a critical ratio r=p(h,y)/q(h,y), define s(h,y)=sign(p(h,y)-r*q(h,y)) in {-1,0,+1}, T={s=0}, and Q_T=sum_T q(h,y). EC48B tests S_K=Z using the graph of all optimum deterministic encoder/decoder pairs, with up to K^|H|*2^(K*|Y|) vertices. The next result contracts away all deterministic decoder enumeration *without changing connected-component tied-mass intervals*.

## Theorem EC48C.1 (exact optimal encoder quotient)
For each deterministic encoder f:H->{1,...,K}, define forced mask d_f(m,y)=+1 if at least one h encoded as m has s(h,y)=+1; d_f(m,y)=-1 if at least one has s=-1; and d_f(m,y)=0 otherwise. Call f admissible precisely when no (m,y) receives both strict signs.

For admissible f define
  L_f = sum_{(h,y) in T, d_f(f(h),y)=+1} q(h,y),
  U_f = Q_T - sum_{(h,y) in T, d_f(f(h),y)=-1} q(h,y).

Build an undirected graph A_r on admissible f. Connect f,g if they differ in exactly one h and all forced entries d_f(m,y),d_g(m,y) agree wherever they are both nonzero. For every connected component C, set L_C=min_{f in C} L_f and U_C=max_{f in C} U_f.

Then the exact tied-mass image of all K-memory policies maximizing support in normal direction (1,-r) is
                 union_C [L_C,U_C].
In particular,
                 S_K=Z  iff  for every distinct critical r, union_C[L_C,U_C]=[0,Q_T].

### Proof
For fixed admissible f, support maximization forces decoder bit b(m,y)=1 at every + mask, 0 at every - mask, and permits any probability in [0,1] at a zero mask. Its optimizing decoder fiber is a connected product of intervals. The tied mass is a linear function on this product, with exactly the image [L_f,U_f]. If both signs occur in one group-column, the support is strictly below full-history optimum; therefore every optimizing deterministic policy has admissible f.

For distinct admissible f,g, the deterministic policy graph of EC48B has an optimal edge changing one encoder assignment and keeping all decoder bits unchanged precisely when f,g differ in that one assignment and there exists a common optimum decoder. Such a decoder exists iff the two forced masks have no opposite nonzero entries. All optimum decoder corners over a fixed encoder f form a connected cube, so contracting this cube yields exactly A_r's connected-component partition. Every original encoder edge is contained in an optimum one-coordinate interpolation because support is affine in that encoder simplex coordinate. The full maximizing parameter set is a finite union of optimum product faces (by multi-affine convex expansion), connected component by connected component. Tied mass is continuous and its extrema are attained at deterministic corners, so its component image is exactly [min L_f,max U_f]. Taking the union proves the first equality. EC48B's exposed-zonotope boundary plus origin-star-shaped argument proves the iff equality. QED.

The graph has at most K^|H| vertices instead of K^|H|*2^(K|Y|). Its construction uses O(K^|H|*[|H||Y|+|H|(K-1)K|Y|]) elementary operations at fixed r with hash-addressable encoders, excluding exact-arithmetic bit costs. No polynomial-time claim is made for varying H or K.

## Corollary EC48C.2 (weight-independent face filling)
If one connected component of A_r contains some f with L_f=0 and some g with U_g=Q_T, then its continuous image is all [0,Q_T]. Moreover this holds for *every strictly positive* assignment of tied-cell q weights: L_f=0 means no tied cell is forced to 1, while U_g=Q_T means no tied cell is forced to 0, both solely combinatorial statements. The graph does not depend on magnitudes of q.

## Corollary EC48C.3 (joint adjacent-sign sufficient bound)
For every r let sigma_low(h,y)=s(h,y) if nonzero and +1 if zero, and sigma_high(h,y)=s(h,y) if nonzero and -1 if zero. Let kappa_r be the number of distinct row pairs (sigma_low(h,*),sigma_high(h,*)). If K>=max_r kappa_r, then S_K=Z.

Proof: group histories by these row pairs. At each group-column, all rows either have the same strict sign or are all tied, so fixed strict decoder bits and a continuously variable tied-only decoder bit fill the entire exposed face. Repeat at each r and apply EC48B's boundary criterion. QED. This sufficient K can exceed the true minimum.

## EC48C.4 — Full small-alphabet classification for K=2
**Finite-alphabet computer-assisted theorem:** For every strictly positive p,q on |H|<=4 and |Y|<=3, if the EC48A generic-threshold signature maximum K_hull <=2, then S_2=Z (not only their convex hull).

At any critical r, the sign matrix s belongs to {-1,0,+1}^{H x Y}. Immediately below r all zero entries behave as +, immediately above r as -. The two resulting distinct-row-profile counts are <=K_hull<=2. Exhaustive enumeration of all 559,344 ternary sign matrices across H=1..4,Y=1..3 checks all 22,614 meeting both profile constraints. For every eligible matrix, the encoder graph has **one connected component** containing both zero and total tied-mass endpoints when q=1. By Corollary EC48C.2 that single component fills the entire face for arbitrary strictly positive q weights, including irrational real weights. Every critical face fills, so S_2=Z. The exact JavaScript checker is saved alongside this proof. This is an exhaustive finite combinatorial certificate, not an infinite-alphabet proof or independent Lean checker.

Eligible counts by (H,Y): (1,1)=3,(2,1)=9,(3,1)=27,(4,1)=81,(2,2)=81,(3,2)=363,(4,2)=1389,(2,3)=729,(3,3)=3867,(4,3)=16065.

An independently implemented Python exact-integer checker (EC48C_VERIFY.py in the accompanying local evidence bundle) compared the contracted graph with the complete EC48B deterministic (f,b) graph in **2,187** exhaustive sign-model instances, with nonuniform positive integer tied weights. All exact component-interval lists matched; no float is used. Neither finite check is a universal theorem beyond its quantified finite domain.

### Explicit weighted example: sufficient joint-signature bound is not sharp
Take P raw counts [[2,2],[2,3],[1,2],[1,3]] and Q raw counts [[2,2],[2,2],[2,2],[2,2]], both sum to 16; normalize each by 16. At r=1 the sign rows are (0,0),(0,+),(-,0),(-,+). The open-threshold signature counts are 2 and 2 (K_hull=2), but four different joint adjacent-sign row pairs exist (kappa_1=4). The K=2 encoder graph nevertheless has an optimum connected component with tied raw Q-mass interval **[0,8]**, hence S_2=Z for this model. Looking only at intervals for fixed deterministic encoders, while omitting stochastic encoder edges, would give a spurious missing-face counterexample.

## Reuse, boundaries, next
BRC positive exact-weight semantics: REUSE_APPLIED. EC48A open-signature law: REUSE_APPLIED, preserving its convex-hull scope. EC48B optimum deterministic graph: EXTEND_EXISTING_TOOL by a mathematically equivalent encoder quotient, with comparison against the original. No new native heartbeat input is generated, no X6 transfer or mathematical acceptance is claimed. P000 and ACTIVE worldview remain unchanged.

**EC48D open problem:** decide whether conv(S_K)=Z implies S_K=Z for arbitrary finite H,Y and K>=2. Extend encoder-component search structurally; either prove face connectivity across all admissible sign matrices or produce an explicit positive-rational counterexample with exact missing tied-mass interval. A separate variable-depth four-observer generalization remains open.
